A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. The main text, figures, tables, C-DIST equation, and Appendices A–G are readable and can be matched across the pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original cultural-adaptation experiments, including multilingual classification, MMLU performance, cross-cultural evaluations, and invalid-response analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports three-run standard deviations for the central comparison in Table 5.

M1.justification: Zero-shot prompting, per-culture LoRA adaptation, training-data combinations, and inference procedures remain unchanged. The q_proj/v_proj targets and dropout newly mentioned in the main text were already documented in v1 Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten linguistic-cultural settings, WVS/Wikipedia/NormAd training sources, multilingual classification datasets, and MMLU evaluation. The new dataset-balance paragraph cites counts already present in Appendix F.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same zero-shot, WVS-only, narrative-only, and combined-data configurations for the same model families. Combined-culture adaptation also remains unchanged in Appendix C.3.

E3.justification: No changes are reported to datasets' splits or sample counts, model sizes, training budgets, prompts, F1/C-DIST metrics, or generation procedures. Added hardware information documents existing experiments; repeated-run reporting is assessed under E5.

E4.justification: The data-source comparisons, embedding visualizations, cross-cultural heatmaps, combined-culture analysis, probability-based evaluations, and invalid-response cases are retained. New Section 5.1 interprets existing evidence rather than introducing an additional ablation or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates and a seed-42 training description. v2 introduces means and standard deviations across three differently seeded runs throughout the central multi-model comparison in Table 5, substantially expanding uncertainty reporting. This is newly reported replication, not an established increase from a documented earlier run count; Appendix B still specifies only seed 42.

E6.justification: Existing point estimates and rankings are unchanged: for example, Llama WVS+NormAd retains C-DIST 0.89, cultural F1 40.94, and MMLU F1 50.43. v2 adds findings about run variability and explicitly asserts statistically significant distinctiveness improvements in most cases, although no significance test or p-values substantiate that assertion.

T1.justification: The performance-matrix definition, column normalization, and C-DIST equation remain unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theorems, proofs, or formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about WVS-related cultural homogenization, factual-knowledge interference, and narrative augmentation. The added code-release statement does not alter the scientific contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds a specific qualification about resource imbalance and strengthens explanations of Wikipedia's factual-stabilization role versus NormAd's behavioral supervision. Sections 5.1 and 6 add practical recommendations for data mixtures. These extend existing interpretations; the formal Limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a code-repository pointer, and Section 3.4 newly discloses a single 80GB A100 GPU and bf16 training. Other highlighted details, including gradient checkpointing and LoRA targets, already appeared in Appendix B.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds discussion of Beck et al. (2024), positioning evaluation-oriented sensitivity studies as complementary to adaptation methods. That work was already cited in v1, and the bibliography otherwise retains the same works.

P1.justification: v2 adds terminology and dataset-balance paragraphs, model-selection rationale, Section 5.1, acknowledgments, and expanded affiliation text, while rewriting the opening of Section 5. The overall organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 5 is reformatted for mean-plus-standard-deviation entries, with revised emphasis and caption. Tables and figures shift relative to surrounding prose, but the figure content and appendix displays are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the existing evidence easier to assess through Table 5's uncertainty reporting, explicit data-imbalance qualifications, and added code-access and hardware information. These provide a limited transparency and reproducibility gain. The improvement is constrained by an unsupported statistical-significance assertion and seed documentation that remains incomplete in Appendix B.
